correctness.rationale: The invariant plane measure has uniform |n_z| and unsigned Lebesgue offset. A previously proven fiber criterion gives an exact annular mark density x W_R(x)/J_R on y<G_R(x)-x. Compact support controls all remainders; differentiability of the meridian support at the vertical direction gives G_R(x)=1+q x/R+o(1/R) uniformly. Hence J_R=1/6+q/(3R)+o(1/R), the universal law and coefficient 2q, with separate q=0 control. A locally C2 support function yields O(R^-2); for a unit disk the beta-integral gives the explicit coefficient 27/400-9 sqrt(30)/2500 with O(R^-4) remainder. The checker passed 109 independent numeric/algebraic assertions; no finite test is used as proof.

value.rationale: The geometry of a rare random annular section is conditioned rather than typical. Its rescaled normal tilt has a universal Beta(2,2) law over all convex symmetric meridians, and the sharp first-order total-variation defect recovers the exposed top-face half-width. Thus the convergence speed provides a meaningful boundary-regularity invariant distinguishing flat-capped and smooth meridians. The circular second-order coefficient quantifies the vanishing-face regime and is not a routine recalculation of a known scalar probability.
